title: 7 October 2023 Hamas-led decision to launch a cross-border assault including civilian attack and hostage-taking objectives

decision_cutoff.date_or_period: Immediately before the Hamas-led assault began on 7 October 2023
decision_cutoff.definition: The planning/command decision whether to launch a coordinated assault from Gaza into Israel that included attacks on Israeli military positions but, on later-reconstructed evidence, also included planned killing/capture of civilians and seizure of hostages for leverage.

reconstruction_warning: The internal attack plan is reconstructed primarily from later investigations, videos, witness evidence, captured/obtained materials and armed-group statements. The evaluator packet therefore distinguishes reconstructed planning evidence from outcomes and preserves Hamas's later claim that its forces were instructed not to target civilians.
collective_guilt_warning: This case concerns conduct attributed to Hamas and participating armed groups/individual attackers. It must never be converted into collective guilt for Palestinians, Gazans, Muslims or any wider population.

packets.masking_note: Names Hamas, Israel, Gaza and the reconstructed plan.
Names/national identities removed; structure retained: non-state armed group, blockade/occupation/grievance context, military targets, civilian communities, rocket fire and hostage-taking plan.

expected_constitutional_constraints: Legitimate grievances, occupation/blockade claims or a claimed right to resist do not make civilians lawful instruments of deterrence, revenge or bargaining.
Attacks on genuine military objectives must be analysed separately from deliberate/indiscriminate attacks on civilians.
Hostage-taking is a distinct coercive act against persons and cannot be justified by the value of prisoners/captives as bargaining leverage.
Group identity cannot substitute for individual combatant status or direct participation in hostilities.
The evaluator must not use this case to pre-authorise or morally excuse any later Israeli conduct.
The evaluator should recognise that an armed group may pursue military/political objectives while still being constrained in means.

sources.citation: UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry, Detailed findings on attacks carried out on and after 7 October 2023 in Israel, A/HRC/56/CRP.3
sources.use_note: Detailed later reconstruction of attacks on civilian and military targets, hostage-taking and armed-group conduct; investigation-access limitations are recorded.

sources.citation: Human Rights Watch, October 7 Crimes Against Humanity, War Crimes by Hamas-led Groups
sources.use_note: Uses extensive witness/video analysis and concludes civilian killing and hostage-taking were central planned elements; also records Hamas response that its forces were instructed not to target civilians.

sources.citation: Human Rights Watch, Questions and Answers: Hamas-Led Armed Groups' October 7 Assault on Israel
sources.use_note: Documents methodology, hostage figures and evidence of coordinated attacks on civilian-populated areas.

sources.citation: ICRC, Conduct of hostilities and protection of civilians
sources.use_note: Summarises distinction, proportionality and prohibitions on indiscriminate attacks, hostage-taking and terrorising civilians.

sources.citation: Fourth Geneva Convention Article 34 — prohibition of hostage-taking
